newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cegetel spending to rival France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Cegetel spending to rival France Telecom.

text.p: Cegetel, the telecommunications unit of Generale des Eaux, is embarking upon a big investment programme to build itself up as a rival to France Telecom even before full market liberalisation in 1998.

Phillipe Germond, managing director, said on Tuesday the company would invest five billion francs ($858.3 million) per year over the next three years in the build-up of its infrastructure system up to the year 2000.
Germond said Cegetel had seven billion francs in cash and could lean on its strong parent groups.
While Generale des Eaux has a total 44 percent stake, British Telecommunications Plc has a 26 percent stake, SBC has an indirect 15 percent and Mannesmann AG a direct 15 percent.
Germond told a news conference on the launch of Cegetel's business services that he expected there to be only one full rival to France Telecom in January 1998.

"The time it takes to build up your infrastructure, we're talking about months, about half-years. I think we will be the only global rival to France Telecom in January 1998 and that gives us a premium," he said.

Bouygues Telecom, with its allies Veba of Germany and Italy's Stet and possibly with Lyonnaise des Eaux, is expected to become France's third overall telecoms operator but the timing of these plans is not yet set.

Germond repeated Cegetel's aim of clinching 20 percent of the French telecommunications market in 10 years. He detailed this goal as getting 40 percent of the mobile telecommunications market, 20 percent of the long distance fixed markets, 30 percent of local traffic in the towns where it operates and 20 percent in data traffic.
Germond said Cegetel aimed to have local loops in one-third of France's towns.

He said that the total French telecommunications market was set to grow to 200 billion francs in 2006, despite massive price cuts, from 122 billion now. The mobile telecoms sector will see the biggest growth, going to 60 billion from 13.4 billion.

Local communications will make up 27 percent of the market in 2006. The long distance market is expected to remain stable at 56 billion francs while data traffic will double to 28 billion francs in 2006 from 13.4 billion in 1996.
Business commmunciations will remain stable at 35 percent of the total market, Germond said.

Cegetel started on Tuesday with offering business services, building upon the British Telecom Pleiade system and the infrastructure backbone of Telecom Developpement, a joint-venture with railways SNCF.
Cegetel is the exclusive distributor of Concert services in France, Concert being the world telecom services alliance of British Telecom and MCI.

The group has put a local loop in place in the La Defense business area of Paris and will in the next two years cover the Hauts de Seine area north-west of Paris, some areas in Paris itself, Lyon, Marseille, Lille and Toulouse.
Richard Lalande, vice-managing director, said Cegetel's services were of a quality that France Telecom could not meet and he said the group aimed to offer better services.
France Telecom has various services for companies, including its Transpac data transfer service and the Global One international alliance with Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp of the U.S..

"Of course we will pitch our prices below that of the market reference, France Telecom. But they will slash their rates as well and in the end the competition will be about who has the best service," Lalande said. ($ = 5.825 French Francs)
